members.name: Members with roles
members.sentence: People sign in and post; the owner makes some of them admins who can moderate.

files.index.html:
Members

The clubhouse

Sign in to read and write posts. The owner decides who is an admin.

Posts
MembersOnly the owner changes roles
files.schema.sql:
-- One row per person who joined. The Kernel says who is signed in and which
-- account is the owner's; the role column is the app's own decision.
-- Staff actions check: (SELECT role FROM profiles WHERE user_id = ?1) IN ('admin', 'owner')
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS profiles (
  user_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  display_name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(display_name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 40),
  role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member' CHECK (role IN ('member', 'admin', 'owner')),
  joined_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS posts (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  author_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  body TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(body)) BETWEEN 1 AND 2000),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

digest.name: Nightly digest
digest.sentence: Members write entries; each morning every member gets an email listing what they wrote the day before.

files.index.html:
Daily log

What happened

Every morning at 07:00 UTC the app emails each member the entries they wrote the day before. Nobody presses a button for it.

Your entries
files.schema.sql:
-- What members write during the day. The nightly digest stamps digested_at
-- on the entries it mailed, so an entry goes out once.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entries (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  body TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(body)) BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  digested_at INTEGER
);
